title: Viktor Frankl and the Search for Meaning
baseline: Working-tree frankl.html captured before this assignment, preserving its pre-existing uncommitted navigation state. Counts are not against HEAD.
word_count_method: Text in main before sources, including headings, card text, citations and caption; excludes hero, sources, navigation, styles and scripts. Word tokens include apostrophes inside words.
editorial_rationale: Replaced a claim that meaning decided camp survival with a concrete manuscript example and an immediate distinction between testimony and causal evidence.

Kept the will to meaning, existential vacuum, personal responsibility, all three meaning categories, paradoxical intention and the happiness argument. Cut repeated summaries, dramatic fragments, motivational commands, sales figures and literary superlatives.
Broadened the second gallery card from romantic love to experience including nature and art. Added the bereaved physician example to show what attitudinal meaning actually looks like.

Removed the recovery-thread conclusion, which flattened Frankl into a secular Serenity Prayer and treated camp experience as a credential settling his claims. The final factual limit is the unverified authorship of the familiar quotation.

Kept the portrait, structural classes, gallery, buttons, keyboard behavior and no-JavaScript authored cards. Changed generated gallery label from in his words to in plain English and explicitly labeled card summaries as paraphrases.

Kept quotes to two unchanged extracts totaling 17 words, linked to specific pages in the verified transcription. Removed approximate paperback pages and the prior claim that quote punctuation had been silently changed.

major_factual_corrections.before: The opening says nothing else changed at Christmas and loss of hope caused increased deaths.
major_factual_corrections.after: The book attributes that interpretation to its camp doctor; the post explains that recollections lack the records needed to isolate despair from hunger, exhaustion and infection.

major_factual_corrections.before: Meaning decided who lived, and those with a reason were the people who held on.
major_factual_corrections.after: Murder, labor, starvation, disease, selection, assistance and chance could decide fate. Survivorship cannot be converted into a claim about the murdered lacking reasons to live.

major_factual_corrections.before: Frankl invented and named logotherapy after returning to Vienna.
major_factual_corrections.after: He used the name in 1926 and began The Doctor and the Soul before deportation. His theory preceded his imprisonment.

major_factual_corrections.before: The wife imagined on the march was already dead.
major_factual_corrections.after: Frankl says he had no way to know whether she was alive. Her death at the time of that scene is not established.

major_factual_corrections.before: The memoir all but proved universally inviolable choice under coercion.
major_factual_corrections.after: The remembered generosity shows some acts were possible, without establishing that every prisoner had the same capacity to choose.

major_factual_corrections.before: The polished stimulus-and-response sentence is Covey's.
major_factual_corrections.after: The institute reports Covey remembered an unrecorded library source; the original author remains unidentified.

major_factual_corrections.before: An Internet Archive link was labeled a 2006 edition.
major_factual_corrections.after: Its record is 1963. Replaced the public citation with Beacon's actual 2006 edition page.

remaining_uncertainties: Date of Tilly Frankl's death relative to the march scene remains unknown; no longer claimed.

Frankl says he wrote the memoir in 1945 in its 1992 preface; institute chronology places nine-day dictation under 1946. The post states only the verified publication year and omits the composition date.
No independent camp mortality records were examined to evaluate the Christmas death-spike interpretation.
No treatment efficacy claim is made from the therapeutic case reports.
The source transcription has not been treated as a facsimile of the named 2006 paperback.
suggested_hub_description: Frankl describes meaning through work, love and unavoidable suffering. His camp memoir shows moments of choice under coercion, while exposing the limits of testimony about survival.
